record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.context_brief: Choquet capacity and morphological random-set constraints in GANs
record.original_question: In generative adversarial networks for image generation or microstructure simulation, can Choquet capacity be used in discriminators to impose morphological constraints learned from empirical data, and can GAN generators incorporate deconvolution-like image simulation closer to morphological random-set models by using morphological layers?

evidence.quote: Can the notion of Choquet capacity play a role in the GAN discriminators to explicitly impose morphological constraints learned from the empirical data? Can one incorporate a ‘deconvolution’ image simulation closer to the morphological random set models into the GAN generators, thanks to the use of morphological layers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a compact Hausdorff space (for example a finite pixel grid $E \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$) and let $\mathcal{F}(E)$ denote the collection of closed subsets of $E$. A Choquet capacity is a functional $T:\mathcal{F}(E)\to[0,1]$ that is increasing ($A\subseteq B\Rightarrow T(A)\le T(B)$), upper semicontinuous on decreasing sequences, and alternating of infinite order. By the Choquet–Matheron theorem, every Choquet capacity $T$ with $T(\emptyset)=0$ corresponds uniquely to the distribution of a random closed set $X$ in $E$ via $T(K)=\mathbb{P}(X\cap K\neq\emptyset)$ for compact $K\subset E$. Morphological random-set models (e.g. Boolean models) generate random images as $X=\bigcup_i (x_i\oplus K_i)$ where $\{x_i\}$ is a point process and $K_i$ are random compact ``grains'', with $\oplus$ denoting Minkowski addition. A morphological neural-network layer is a map built from elementary operations of dilation $(f\oplus g)(x)=\sup_y\{f(y)+g(x-y)\}$ and erosion $(f\ominus g)(x)=\inf_y\{f(y+x)-g(y)\}$ with learnable structuring functions $g$.

Consider a generative adversarial network (GAN) consisting of a generator $G_\theta:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathcal{F}(E)$ and a discriminator $D_\phi:\mathcal{F}(E)\to\mathbb{R}$, trained on samples of a target random closed set $X^\star$ with associated Choquet capacity $T^\star$.

(a) Construct a discriminator architecture in which the functional implemented by $D_\phi$ is, or contains as a component, an empirical Choquet-capacity functional $\widehat T_\phi$ on $\mathcal{F}(E)$ (i.e., a learnable map satisfying the monotonicity, upper semicontinuity and alternation-of-infinite-order axioms), and prove that minimizing the resulting adversarial loss enforces convergence of the Choquet capacity of $G_\theta$ to $T^\star$ in an appropriate metric (such as the Prokhorov-type metric on capacities).

(b) Construct a generator architecture composed of morphological layers (compositions of learnable dilations and erosions) and a stochastic point-process input such that $G_\theta$ realizes, in the limit of suitable depth/width, an arbitrary Boolean random-set model on $E$; equivalently, show that morphological-layer generators are universal approximators for random closed sets whose grain distributions lie in a prescribed class.

Determine whether both constructions (a) and (b) are achievable, and exhibit explicit architectures and training criteria for which the resulting GAN provably converges (in distribution of random closed sets) to the target morphological random-set model.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a programmatic research direction proposing the integration of Choquet capacity functionals into GAN discriminators and morphological layers into GAN generators for random-set image simulation. Searches reveal active but partial work on morphological neural networks and on GANs for microstructure simulation, but no result that establishes both (a) a Choquet-capacity-based discriminator with provable capacity-convergence guarantees and (b) a universal-approximation result for Boolean random sets via morphological generator layers. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era
status_evidence.snippet: Posed as an open question regarding the role of Choquet capacity and morphological layers in GANs.
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open research question.
